commit.message:
chore(deploy): increase production node CPU capacity (#1746)

Production PostgreSQL is CPU-starved on its shared two-vCPU node. Set
`mcp-registry:nodeMachineType` to `e2-standard-4` for production only;
staging retains its `e2-standard-2` default from #1745. Keep two nodes,
application 1.8.5, PostgreSQL resources and buffers, connection limits,
cache policy, and disks unchanged.

The full production preview with workflow-pinned Pulumi 3.188.0 shows a
node-pool update (not pool replacement), plus existing deployment
housekeeping. The single registry/Grafana database instances will be
interrupted as nodes are replaced; ingress caches will also warm again.
Surge quota and the latest verified production backup were checked.

After rollout, verify node types, database readiness/reconnection and
placement, then compare CPU pressure, pool backlog, listing latency, and
errors under comparable traffic. A machine-type rollback is another
disruptive node rollout. Merge after the #1745 staging deployment and
final checks pass.

commit.message:
chore(deploy): configure GCP node size per environment (#1745)

Production CPU contention requires additional node capacity without
increasing staging costs. Add `mcp-registry:nodeMachineType`, defaulting
to the existing `e2-standard-2`, so production can be promoted
independently in a subsequent configuration-only change. Neither stack
is resized by this PR.

Document node replacement, singleton database interruption, cold-cache
behavior, comparison metrics, and disruptive rollback.

Validation: `make -C deploy build`, `git diff --check`, and independent
code review pass. Full staging and production previews with
workflow-pinned Pulumi 3.188.0 pass and show no node-pool change.
Expected deployment housekeeping remains: the application
deployment-commit annotation, two recreated ingress admission Jobs, and
existing Grafana RBAC normalization. No database, disk, cache-policy, or
application-image changes.

commit.message:
chore(deploy): promote production to 1.8.5 (#1744)

Promote production from `1.8.4` to `1.8.5` to collect request
arrivals/backlog, database acquisition/query metrics, and bounded
per-request slow-listing diagnostics from #1742 and #1743. The
infrastructure deployment also appends cache status and upstream timings
to ingress logs.

The released commit is `ad119f3d478a936c95d73b291c5fbc106231f7bc`. This
release also includes publisher and validator fixes merged since v1.8.4.
No new database migration is included.

Validation:
- Diagnostic implementation CI passed, including integration tests and
code analysis.
- [Staging
rollout](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/actions/runs/40335967054)
passed. Both new replicas are ready with zero restarts. Bounded
seven-second table-lock tests produced progress and completion
diagnostics whose backend PIDs matched PostgreSQL `Lock/relation` waits.
Direct app cancellation emitted outcome `canceled` and status 499;
ingress request IDs matched app logs. Diagnostic events reached Cloud
Logging. No staging rows were changed.
- [v1.8.5 release
workflow](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/actions/runs/40337658869)
passed. Verified the published `1.8.5` OCI index contains Linux amd64
and arm64 images; digest
`sha256:f3e30c6feeb229988e3d21e085b317f74b6dcfb826b91e548a18188e5e3beb9a`.
- Refreshed production preview at promotion commit `c2a49ba` succeeded
against a local copy of production state: application Deployment
image/annotation update, ingress log-format ConfigMap replacement, two
admission setup Jobs recreated, and existing Grafana RBAC normalization.
No node, database, or persistent-volume changes are planned.

Merge triggers the production deployment. Verify both new application
replicas, metric ingestion, ingress log fields, and API health after
deployment. PostgreSQL's internal waits still require contemporaneous
database sampling; diagnostic logs are rate-limited samples.

Application rollback: restore `imageTag` to `1.8.4`. The ingress logging
suffix remains unless separately reverted.

Pre-deployment baseline at 14:14 UTC on October 26: listing p95
approximately 2.3s, 5xx approximately 0.26%, and later live samples
showed BufferMapping contention. This degradation predates the
promotion. A bounded read-only PostgreSQL activity capture is running
across the rollout.

commit.message:
feat(observability): diagnose individual slow listing requests (#1743)

Slow listing requests currently expose separate HTTP and database
histograms, but there is no request-level timing record. Database timing
also includes application JSON decoding, making a slow query
indistinguishable from slow row processing.

Add bounded structured diagnostics for GET `/v0/servers` and
`/v0.1/servers`: progress after 2 seconds and every 10 seconds while
outstanding, plus completion for slow or failed requests. Records
correlate ingress request ID, pod, route, query-shape flags, page size,
PostgreSQL backend PID and SQLSTATE, row/JSON-byte counts, and exclusive
handler/acquisition/query/fetch/decode/response timings. Raw SQL,
arguments, cursors, search strings and payloads are excluded. Logging is
capped per pod at 2 events/second with burst 10 and suppression
accounting; fast successful requests remain silent.

Validation:
- Full internal/cmd unit suite passed with race detection and coverage
against PostgreSQL 17.
- Controlled tests prove a blocked pool is visible before cancellation,
delayed queries are distinct from row processing, timings account for
the full request, and request IDs/context propagate through the real
Huma adapter.
- Tests cover SQLSTATE-only error detail, panic/cancellation completion,
timer shutdown and bounded log volume.
- `make lint`, `make build`, `make validate`, and `git diff --check`
passed.

Follow-up to #1742. No query, index, resource, or cache-policy changes.
After staging deployment, verify a bounded slow request and log
ingestion before cutting the production release. Internal PostgreSQL
wait attribution still requires contemporaneous database samples;
sampled logs are not exhaustive tracing.

commit.message:
feat(observability): expose request backlog and database waits (#1742)

When handlers stall, the existing request counter falls because it
counts completions, hiding incoming demand and backlog growth. Ingress
logs also omit cache outcomes, making duplicate upstream work difficult
to distinguish from database contention.

This adds application arrival and in-flight metrics, pgx pool
acquisition timing/pending counts and connection gauges, and query
timing after acquisition through row consumption. Database labels use
bounded operation/outcome values without SQL or parameters. Existing
completion metrics retain their semantics. Pool callbacks are
unregistered on close, and failed startup pools are cleaned up.

Ingress access logs retain their existing combined-log prefix and append
cache status, scheme/host, controller pod, upstream connection/header
timing, and a millisecond completion timestamp. The runbook explains
measurement limits, PromQL queries, and how to correlate cache and
database evidence. Existing log parsers anchored to the end of the old
format must accept the suffix; ingress logs remain in the existing GKE
logging destination rather than being added to VictoriaLogs.

Validation:
- Full internal/cmd unit suite with race detection and coverage against
temporary local PostgreSQL 17.
- New tests for blocked-handler arrivals, cancellation/panic cleanup,
canceled pool waits, query timing through row close, and bounded labels.
- `make lint`, `make validate`, `make build`, and `make -C deploy build`
passed.
- Local application smoke checks verified exported metrics for all four
list operation classes and in-flight drainage.
- GitHub CI passed, including the Docker-based integration tests,
build/lint/validation, govulncheck, and Go/Python/Actions analysis.

Application metrics require an application release/promotion; cache log
fields require infrastructure promotion. No changes to cache policy,
concurrency limits, SQL/indexes, or production configuration were
applied.

commit.message:
deploy: promote balanced node disks to production (#1740)

Promote the 50 GB `pd-balanced` node boot disks from #1739 through the
existing production workflow while retaining registry application image
`1.8.4`. This comment-only change to `deploy/Pulumi.gcpProd.yaml`
deliberately triggers that workflow on merge. The two-node pool retains
`e2-standard-2` machines and uses surge upgrades with one extra node and
zero unavailable nodes.

Staging rollout succeeded:
https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/actions/runs/40243009855.
Verified both original nodes were replaced with Ready nodes whose actual
boot disks are 50 GB `pd-balanced`. All four original persistent volumes
retain their identities, volume handles and sizes, and both PostgreSQL
clusters recovered. Every active workload is ready; the two registry
replicas are on different nodes, and registry/ingress containers have
zero restarts. Health, listing and name-search checks returned HTTP 200
in about 0.6 seconds; a fresh unique search also returned HTTP 200.

**Allow for a multi-minute database interruption when merging.** During
staging replacement, registry PostgreSQL was unready from 23:16:45 to
23:20:29 UTC on October 25 (3m44s), including its configured 180-second
smart-shutdown timeout before disk reattachment/startup. This is an
observed staging duration, not a production guarantee. Grafana
PostgreSQL also moved. The single staging ingress replica caused three
failed health samples during its move; production has two ingress
replicas but still only one instance of each database. `/health` does
not query PostgreSQL, so database readiness was checked separately.
Surge capacity does not provide database HA.

Refreshed production Pulumi preview at `c71e488`, after #1738 deployed,
passed: node-pool boot-disk size/type update, registry deploy-commit
annotation update, recreation of two automatically cleaned-up ingress
admission Jobs, and existing Grafana empty-rule normalization. No Pulumi
resource deletions/replacements or database/persistent-volume changes.
GKE nevertheless replaces the node VMs incrementally. All PR CI checks
passed.

Check the latest successful registry backup when merging; it last
succeeded at 2026-10-25 04:47:13 UTC during preparation. Both projects
have surge quota headroom; actual zonal capacity is established during
provisioning.

After production rollout, verify both nodes have 50 GB balanced boot
disks, all original persistent volumes are retained, both databases
recover, and workloads/API smoke checks pass. Compare disk queues,
ingress restarts and request latency during busy traffic before
concluding that #1252 is resolved.
